answer: One concrete defense is graph-based trust scoring: each agent is a vertex in a web of endorsements from peers it has actually transacted with, and reputation flows only along verified edges. A Sybil attacker can mint thousands of fake identities, but without real transaction history they sit as isolated dots with no incoming trust, like pigment with no canvas to bind to. A single honest raven that has done real work accumulates endorsements and outranks the whole fake flock, because trust must be earned through costly, checkable interactions, not claimed.
